fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not escape G13: generalized Hamming weights constrain codewords, not arbitrary integral affine combinations of encoded columns. The fixed Golay test lacks a frozen basis, target, coupling, weights, and full-fiber solver, and a constant code cannot address G14/G20/G21 scaling.

Proposal 2 assumes the missing support lemma. A k-perfect hash isolates only supports of size at most k, while a parity on k+1 variables remains a degree-width blind spot; sparse linear expander measurements can also have high-support integral kernels. The eight-variable test is unfrozen and cannot discriminate the claimed asymptotic handoff.

Proposal 3 is not a finite search as stated: integral Gram entries, targets, port representatives, state classes, scale, gluing maps, and coefficient bounds are unspecified. Moreover, additive min-plus costs do not automatically yield a multiplicative rho-per-level gap, so even a depth-two pass would not establish the asserted recurrence.

Proposal 4 supplies no formula-to-relative-class map and no proof that mod-2 cosystolic expansion controls shortest integral representatives under unrestricted carries. The fundamental group of RP2 has only a double cover, so the proposed finite example cannot test polynomial cover growth or G20/G21 amplification.

Proposal 5 amplifies only nonzero residuals and therefore leaves G7/G13/G19 exact kernels untouched; fixed linear embeddings preserve affine collisions. On the proposed nine-clause encoding, the already verified zero-residual signed selector forces alpha=0, so the p=17 test would merely reproduce a known blocker.

Proposal 6 gives no theorem by which M-convexity enforces nonnegative path decomposition over an unrestricted integer flow fiber. Laminar inventories are linear aggregates that affine or signed splices may preserve, and even an O(log L) inventory penalty is negligible against an Omega(L) completeness radius without a scale-stable recurrence. The graph segment, Gram matrices, target, and unrestricted solver are not frozen.

G19 verifies an exact accepting signed flow with two negative coefficients and zero residual; obstruction and control squared minima are 22770 and 22754.

G9/G11 exhibit constant-cost parity kernels, while G12 shows that charging parity can expose a cheaper clause drop. Every shell or fingerprint proposal must audit both in the complete unrestricted fiber.
G5 found squared-norm-at-most-four overlap circuits in every tested private-row composition, so local isolation does not imply compositional soundness.
G14 is only a finite shell pass through B+32. No supplied verifier proves recursive closure, polynomial relative-gap growth, or an n^c approximation factor.
The six proposals provide no new verifier output and several proposed searches omit enough finite data that they are not executable bounded experiments.
